uncited: The pipeline operates in a multi-stage sequence: Block Selection, Classification, Indexing, Cell Selection, and Mesh Generation (split into Vertex and Face phases).
It relies on a regular grid definition and specific lookup tables to decouple stages and ensure manifold connectivity.
*   **Input:** A regular 3D grid $L$ of scalar values $v_{i,j,k}$, an isovalue $\alpha$, and block-level min/max density bounds.
The mesh is a manifold surface with 1-ring neighbor information available per vertex.
The method uses static lookup tables (precomputed) and dynamic tables (generated per volume).
**Case Table:** Dimensions $(N_x - 1) \times (N_y - 1) \times (N_z - 1)$.
**Index Table:** Dimensions $(N_x - 1) \times (N_y - 1) \times (N_z - 1)$.
*   $v_{i,j,k} > \alpha$ is classified as **inside**.
The total buffer sizes are the sum of the last elements of the transformed arrays.
The following pseudocode outlines the pipeline stages.
It assumes a GPU execution model where thread groups map to blocks.
*   **Unconnected Primitives:** Standard parallel processing produces unconnected primitives because cells are analyzed independently.
*   **Performance Penalties:** Complex QEF minimization using pseudoinverse leads to performance penalties due to limited register counts on parallel hardware.
*   **Time Complexity:** The pipeline is dominated by parallel scan and grid traversal.
The scan is $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of cells.
Mesh generation is proportional to the number of surface cells.
*   **Memory Complexity:** The method uses static lookup tables and dynamic Case/Index tables of size $(N_x - 1) \times (N_y - 1) \times (N_z - 1)$.
*   **Strengths:** Generates manifold surfaces with full 1-ring connectivity; suitable for interactive applications; parallelizable.
*   **Limitations:** Lower vertex quality compared to full QEF minimization (though sufficient for terrain); higher memory usage due to lookup tables.
It was developed to address the lack of interactivity and connectivity in standard parallel surface extraction.

It builds on [Parallel Processing and Pipeline Optimization](6411-parallel-processing-and-pipeline-optimization.md) by applying the shared two-phase (counting/generation) approach with specific optimizations for DMC.
